eberspaecher.title: Simulated parking-heater installation offer test
eberspaecher.setup: In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited camper-van and motorhome owners interested in a diesel parking heater were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical heater, brand, heat output, total installed price, warranty and delivery time. One offer included fitting by a certified mobile technician at the owner's home on a booked date; the other required the owner to book the same fitting at a dealer workshop. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount.
eberspaecher.outcome: paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days
eberspaecher.result: There were {treatment} deposits for the mobile-fitting offer and {control} for the workshop offer.
eberspaecher.limits: This tests whether installation friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at today's prices, that mobile fitting can be staffed or earns a margin, or that it would win buyers from cheaper self-fitted heaters. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.
eberspaecher.relevant: Owners who must arrange fitting at a workshop give up, so a heater offered with fitting at home is bought more often.
eberspaecher.unrelated: Owners buy the brand because it signals reliability to other campers.
